newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says China imposes 13 pct tariff on rice.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says China imposes 13 pct tariff on rice.

text.p: A senior Thai commerce ministry official on Friday said China had imposed a 13 percent tariff on Thai fragrant rice.
But despite the tariff, China's demand for Thai top grade rice remained strong, said Siriphol Yodmuangchareon, deputy director general of internal trade department.
"The amount of (total) fragrant rice exports this year should be similar to that of last year or around 1.45 million tonnes," Siriphol told reporters.
"We noticed that orders from China continue to be active despite the 13 percent tariff," he added.
Thailand projected that it will be able to sell 5.5 million tonnes of rice this year and retain its status as the world's biggest rice exporter.
China imported 631,180 tonnes of rice from Thailand in 1996 of which 465,092 tonnes were fragrant rice.
Thailand encouraged traders to sell more top quality rice as market share for lower quality grade is being bitten into by lower-cost producers such as Vietnam, Pakistan and India.
Siriphol said the price of fragrant rice was high because the output was likely to be lower than expected.
He said the fragrant rice output is likely to drop by four million tonnes from last year.
"And that will definitely affect the price," he said, adding it will ease with the advent of the second crop rice later this month.
Thai 100 percent fragrant rice is indicated at around $685-690 per tonne FOB Bangkok.
